XIRR −18.5% hai, jo annualised return dikhata hai.

XIRR is an annualised return: it takes the date of each instalment into account and expresses the result as a yearly rate. In the first few months of a SIP, even a small rupee change gets stretched to a full-year rate, so XIRR can look very large. Your XIRR is −18.5% per year. XIRR describes the past; it is not a forecast.

You have invested ₹10,000 and currently hold 412.15 units. The current value is ₹9,504, which is ₹496 below the amount invested. Regarding your SIP, you have four options. Pause means no instalments for a chosen period, and it restarts later. Skip means missing only the next instalment. Change amount updates future instalments to a new value. Stop cancels all future instalments. In all these cases, the units you already hold remain in the fund. I cannot recommend whether to take any of these actions. The decision is yours.
